mappings.modals.manage.form.domain.label: Domain
mappings.modals.manage.form.subdomain.er: Subdomain must contain only letters, numbers, and hyphens.
mappings.modals.manage.form.domain.hint: Subdomain is optional. Enter * to match all subdomains (e.g. *.myapp.local matches api.myapp.local).
mappings.modals.manage.form.domain.error: Please enter a valid domain name.
Enter a valid domain name (letters, numbers, hyphens).
mappings.modals.manage.form.host.label: Target Host
mappings.modals.manage.form.host.hint: Host your service listens on. Usually localhost or 127.0.0.1.
mappings.modals.manage.form.port.label: Target Port
mappings.modals.manage.form.port.hint: The localhost port your service listens on.
mappings.modals.manage.form.port.error: Please enter a port between 1 and 65535.
mappings.modals.manage.form.https.label: Backend server uses HTTPS
mappings.modals.manage.form.https.hint: Enable only if your backend service itself runs HTTPS. Leave off for plain HTTP backends (even if the domain is accessed via HTTPS).
mappings.modals.manage.form.mocksEnabled: When enabled, requests matching a mock rule for this domain return the mocked response instead of reaching the backend.
mappings.modals.manage.form.headers.requ: Extra headers sent to the backend with each request (e.g. Authorization, X-Api-Key).
mappings.modals.manage.form.headers.resp: Extra headers added to responses sent back to the browser (e.g. Access-Control-Allow-Origin).
mappings.modals.manage.form.headers.name: Header name
mocks.title: Mocks
mocks.subtitle: Return canned responses for matching requests instead of hitting the backend
mocks.emptyHint: Add a mock to return a canned response for requests matching a method and path pattern. Mocking applies to HTTP and HTTPS requests; it does not affect WebSocket upgrades or raw tunnels.

mocks.modals.export.description: Choose which mocks to include in the exported file.

mocks.modals.manage.form.mapping.label: Domain Mapping
mocks.modals.manage.form.method.label: Method
mocks.modals.manage.form.path.label: Path Pattern
mocks.modals.manage.form.path.hint: Regular expression matched against the request path (without the query string).
mocks.modals.manage.form.status.label: Status Code
mocks.modals.manage.form.status.hint: HTTP status code returned for matching requests.
mocks.modals.manage.form.status.error: Please enter a status code between 100 and 599.
mocks.modals.manage.form.headers.label: Response Headers
mocks.modals.manage.form.headers.hint: Headers added to the mocked response (e.g. Content-Type, Access-Control-Allow-Origin).
mocks.modals.manage.form.body.label: Response Body
mocks.modals.manage.form.body.hint: Body returned for matching requests. Supports dynamic placeholders: {{timestamp}}, {{uuid}}, {{isoDate}}, {{request.method}}, {{request.path}}, {{request.body}}, {{request.host}}, {{request.header.Name}}, {{match.N}} (regex capture groups).
mocks.modals.manage.form.delay.label: Response Delay
mocks.modals.manage.form.delay.hint: Milliseconds to wait before sending the response (0–30000). Use to simulate slow or flaky backends.
mocks.modals.manage.form.delay.error: Please enter a delay between 0 and 30000 milliseconds.
mocks.modals.manage.help.title: Path Pattern Examples
mocks.modals.manage.help.intro: Path patterns are regular expressions matched against the request path, without the query string. Click the copy icon to copy a pattern to the clipboard.
mocks.modals.manage.help.examples.anySeg: Matches any value within a single path segment
mocks.modals.manage.help.examples.prefix: Matches a path and everything beneath it
mocks.modals.manage.help.examples.altern: Matches either of two specific paths
log.title: Request Log
log.subtitle: Live view of requests proxied through Saeng
log.exportHar.dialog.title: Export HAR
log.emptyHint: Requests proxied through Saeng will appear here while the proxy is running.
log.detail.enableHeaders: Enable header logging in Settings to capture headers.
log.detail.enableBody: Enable body logging in Settings to capture response bodies.
settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Configure proxy behaviour and SSL certificates
settings.preferences.title: Preferences
settings.preferences.colorMode.label: Color Mode
settings.preferences.colorMode.descripti: Color mode used in the interface.
settings.preferences.language.label: Language
settings.preferences.language.descriptio: Display language for the Saeng interface.
settings.preferences.iconMode.label: Icon Mode
settings.preferences.iconMode.descriptio: Control where the app icon appears
settings.proxy.title: Proxy
settings.proxy.httpsEnabled.label: Enable HTTPS (SSL termination)
settings.proxy.httpsEnabled.description: Intercept HTTPS traffic with a local CA cert. Requires browser trust step below.
settings.proxy.startOnLaunch.label: Start proxy on launch
settings.proxy.startOnLaunch.description: Automatically start the proxy when Saeng opens.
settings.requestLogs.title: Request Logs
settings.requestLogs.logRequests.label: Log requests
settings.requestLogs.logRequests.descrip: Record proxied requests in the request log.
settings.requestLogs.logMaxEntries.label: Log entries to keep
settings.requestLogs.logMaxEntries.descr: Number of recent requests to keep in the request log ({min}-{max}).
settings.requestLogs.logHeaders.label: Log headers
settings.requestLogs.logHeaders.descript: Capture request and response headers in the request log. Off by default — headers can include sensitive data such as cookies and auth tokens.
settings.requestLogs.logBody.label: Log bodies
settings.requestLogs.logBody.description: Capture request and response bodies in the request log (up to {size} KB each). Off by default — bodies can be large or contain sensitive data.
settings.healthChecks.title: Health Checks
settings.healthChecks.enableCheck.label: Enable backend health checks
settings.healthChecks.enableCheck.descri: Periodically ping each mapping's host:port and show a status indicator next to the domain.
settings.healthChecks.interval.label: Check interval
settings.healthChecks.interval.descripti: How often to ping each backend, in seconds ({min}-{max}).
settings.healthChecks.timeout.label: Check timeout
settings.healthChecks.timeout.descriptio: How long to wait for a response before marking a check as failed, in milliseconds ({min}-{max}).
settings.cert.title: SSL Certificate Authority
settings.cert.description: To serve HTTPS on local domains, Saeng generates a local CA certificate. You must install and trust it in your system keychain once.
settings.cert.confirm.regenerate: This will delete the current CA certificate and all per-domain certificates. You will need to re-trust the new certificate in your browser. Continue?
settings.cert.confirm.delete: This will remove the CA certificate from your trust store and delete all certificate files. HTTPS will not work until you regenerate and re-trust a new certificate. Continue?
settings.cert.platformNote.mac: On macOS: installs into System Keychain (requires your password).
settings.cert.platformNote.windows: On Windows: runs certutil with UAC elevation.
settings.cert.platformNote.linux: On Linux: add the CA certificate to your system trust store manually.
settings.cert.platformNote.unknown: Add the CA certificate to your system trust store manually.

flash.ca.deleted: CA certificate deleted and removed from trust store.
flash.ca.trust.linux: Linux trust management not supported. Please add the CA certificate to your system trust store manually.

flash.ca.untrust.windows: Failed to untrust CA on Windows. This is not an error
